intro: There is no motor, no sensor and no app, so almost nothing can break. Omega Paw's instruction is simple: roll the box over onto its top and back again, and the waste ends up in the pull-out tray. Most problems come from the litter or from how it is rolled.

facts.text: Needs no liners, filters or electricity.
Rolled over onto its top and back, a patented sifting grate drops waste into a pull-out tray.

symptoms.title: Clumps stay in the litter after rolling
symptoms.summary: You roll the box but waste does not reach the tray.
causes: The litter does not clump firmly enough to survive the roll.
The box was not rolled all the way onto its top.

fixes.detail: The grate only works with clumps that hold together.
Roll the box right over onto its top, pause, then roll it back.

symptoms.escalate: There is no mechanism to fail; if clumps still stay put, change the litter.

symptoms.title: Litter collects at the join
symptoms.summary: Material builds up where the two halves meet.
causes: The locking clips are not fully closed, widening the seam.

fixes.detail: Press each locking clip fully home, and wash both halves periodically.

symptoms.escalate: This is routine maintenance for a two-piece box, not a fault.
